title: FIDO2 development authenticator capability and non-production boundary
summary: The package implements a useful FIDO_2_0 development authenticator over USB HID/CTAPHID, including real Ed25519 credential keypairs and signatures, but deterministic credential seed derivation and development presence/attestation mean it is not a production hardware-security or certification claim.
invariants: Advertised protocol version is FIDO_2_0; do not claim CTAP 2.1/2.2/2.3 features that are absent.
Implemented CTAP2 commands include authenticatorGetInfo, authenticatorMakeCredential and authenticatorGetAssertion.
CTAPHID implements INIT, PING, CBOR, framing/assembly, channel allocation and HID-layer errors.
COSE algorithm -8 is EdDSA/Ed25519 and signatures are produced through ooRexx Crypto.
Development credential seed derivation is deterministic and unsuitable for production security.
Development attestation is none; no production attestation private key is embedded.
FidoAlwaysPresent is a development presence provider, not a physical user-presence proof.
CTAP1/U2F, PIN/UV, credential management, large blobs/extensions, reset/configuration and getNextAssertion are not currently implemented.
procedure: Preserve protocol honesty: advertise only implemented capabilities.
For production hardware, replace entropy/key storage, user presence and attestation behind their existing semantic boundaries rather than rewriting CTAPHID/USB semantics.

provenance.claim: README records implemented CTAPHID/CTAP2 behavior, algorithm, semantic events and deliberate development limitations.
Architecture records deterministic credential generation as a development-only security boundary.
